incident-bot: :rotating_light: PagerDuty: PAGER fired for inference-queue.backlog.high (alert_id: pd_48291)

incident-bot: Summary: Inference queue backlog exceeded 60k across us-west-2 cells; autoscaler not scaling fast enough. Possible KV-cache warmup stall. Docs/runbook: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/inference-queue

incident-bot: Alert details:
- metric: inference_queue.backlog_count > 60000 for 2m
- affected services: inference-dispatcher, kv-cache, scale-controller
- severity: P1
- link: https://pagerduty.com/incidents/pd_48291

pagerduty: PagerDuty: Incident pd_48291 - inference-queue.backlog.high has fired. Assigned to on-call rotation: eva-oncall.

eva-oncall: Ack'd on PD and in thread. I'm looking. First pass: checking autoscaler metrics + recent deploys.

frank: Seeing large tail latency on embeddings too. Client error rate up ~0.8%. Customers reporting slow responses. Any recent config flips?

carla: No deploys in last hour. We did push a kernel-optimizer change 3h ago but rollout completed earlier.

dinesh: Pulled metrics:
```
# prometheus query (last 10m)
max(inference_queue.backlog_count) = 61234
scale_controller.pending_nodes = 0
scale_controller.launch_rate = 0.1/s
autoscaler.reconcile_latency = 90s
kv_cache.miss_rate = 0.65
```
Looks like reconcile is slow and launch rate throttled. Provider quotas look okay.

eva-oncall: Running quick health checks on node pool and kube API. Also checking for collision with spot eviction waves.

eva-oncall: kubectl get pods -n inference | grep dispatcher
```
dispatcher-7564b9c7  3/3  Running  0  5m
queue-worker-0     0/2  CrashLoopBackOff  5   4m
queue-worker-1     2/2  Running  0  10m
```
queue-worker-0 is crashing on startup (OOM during cache restore). Might be warmup causing backlog.

frank: If workers fail to boot, autoscaler might think capacity is up and not launch more. Can you check node readiness and kube-scheduler events?

dinesh: Events show a flurry of pull-image and back-off + an API 429 to cloud provider around the time autoscaler tried to provision extra instances:
```
E0908 140211  k8s_provisioner.go:273  provider API rate limit exceeded
Warning  FailedCreate  pod/queue-worker-0  2m (x8 over 5m)  kubelet  Error: failed to create container
```
So provider-side throttling + startup crash.

sre-runbook-bot: Runbook suggestion: try manual scale + temporary bypass of warmup step. Commands: 
```
# scale worker deployment to 6 replicas
kubectl -n inference scale deploy/queue-worker --replicas=6
# temporarily disable cache-restore via config override
kubectl -n inference create configmap temp-no-restore --from-literal=kv_restore=false || true
# force new rollout
kubectl -n inference rollout restart deployment/queue-worker
```

eva-oncall: I'm going to try manual scale to get capacity up. Doing kubectl scale now.

eva-oncall: kubectl -n inference scale deploy/queue-worker --replicas=6  -> accepted

incident-bot: PagerDuty: ack recorded (eva-oncall). Escalation timer paused.

carla: I can toggle the cache-restore flag if needed. If we skip restore some instances might boot faster but miss cached KV prefixes; that will raise token cost temporarily.

frank: Agreed. Do it, prioritize getting workers up to reduce client errors.

dinesh: Executing configmap patch to disable restore for this rollout.
```
kubectl -n inference patch deployment queue-worker --patch '{"spec":{"template":{"metadata":{"annotations":{"kv-restore":"disabled-temp-2026-09-08"}}}}}'
```

dinesh: rollout status shows some pods still CrashLoopBackOff but new pods are coming up.

eva-oncall: Monitoring backlog. Prometheus shows backlog starting to drop: 61k -> 34k in 4m. Latency for embeddings dropping from 2.4s -> 1.1s. Errors going down.

frank: Nice. Customer-facing errors still present for a small cohort; routing fallback enabled for critical customers. Which customers affected? Carla, can you pull the list?

carla: Quick query on logs: top 3 customers by 5xx volume: org-acme, org-zenith, org-sprint. Support notified for org-acme and org-zenith.

eva-oncall: I'm going to leave autoscaler paused for a few minutes while new pods stabilize, then re-enable full autoscaler. Any objections?

frank: thumbs up. Keep an eye on provider API rate limit — we may need to throttle scale requests or stagger.

incident-bot: PagerDuty: PD note: manual scale in progress. Please update incident timeline when stable.

dinesh: Backlog now 12k and falling. Auto-scaler reconcile latency improved to 12s after reducing pressure.

eva-oncall: Re-enabling autoscaler reconcile. Setting cooldown to 60s and max_launch_rate lowered to 0.5/s for the next 15m.

carla: Noted. Filing follow-up ticket to investigate warmup sequence reliability + provider rate limiting. Will include reproducer and timeline.

frank: I'll draft a customer-facing blurb for support: short apology + note about degraded responses while we recovered; will route to sales escalation channels for org-acme.

eva-oncall: Closing PD once metrics stable for 10m. Leaving thread for handoff to next on-call.

sre-runbook-bot: Postmortem checklist suggested: capture heap dumps from crash-loop pods, record provider 429 timestamps, review autoscaler settings and warmup healthcheck.

eva-oncall: Last check: backlog 5.7k, errors back to baseline. I'll close PD in 8m unless regression. Thanks all. :tada:
